summary: Owner request (2026-11-05, #1010): source and defend the two open bridges of WF-FAILS-AS-DESCRIPTION-OF-CATHOLIC-PRACTICE. Pinned and read: Dei Filius ch. 4 and canons IV (Latin, vatican.va), CIC 1983 cann. 747-755 and 1364-1369 (Latin, vatican.va; Book VI as revised 2021), Summa contra Gentiles I.2 n.2-I.3 n.2 (Corpus Thomisticum), PU §373 (pinned German), SEP Fideism §3. (a) is supported by the practice's law of teaching (can. 749 §2), membership (cann. 750-751, 1364-1365), its self-description (Dei Filius ch. 4, can. IV.3 on the declared sense of dogma) and Wittgenstein's 'Theologie als Grammatik'; (b) by Dei Filius ch. 4 (two orders distinct in principle; God known by the gentiles) and SCG I.2-3 (natural reason to which all must assent, against pagans; the philosophers' proofs). The fideist replies are recorded at full strength as unattributed alternatives (conciliar teaching is theology, not grammar; natural reason within a theological horizon), with the supports they have (Phillips 2005, 75; Clayton and Taylor) and the texts against them as attacks. Rejected: recording either bridge as stated (no text states it; each source leaves a named gap) or the attacks as refutations (their premises are stated, not established).
blocker: Both bridges stay open. To count, each needs its recorded fideist reply refuted from established premises; the deciding question for (a), who fixes a practice's grammar, has no vocabulary yet, and a pinned patristic witness on lumen naturale is the next source step for (b).
